claims.text: The alloy's low density is due to formation of a stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
The alloy's mechanical strength is enhanced by a stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
The alloy's corrosion resistance is enhanced by a stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
The alloy's high-temperature oxidation resistance is enhanced by a stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
The precipitate structure enhances grain-boundary strengthening.
The precipitate structure inhibits dislocation movement.
The material to be tested has the nominal composition (FeCoCrNi)0.9Al0.1.
Annealing at 800°C for 100 hours under vacuum will produce precipitates with an average size below 50 nm.
Dislocation pinning contributes to strengthening in the annealed alloy.
Oxide-scale formation contributes to corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The annealed alloy will have higher yield strength than the unannealed baseline alloy.
The annealed alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the unannealed baseline alloy.
The annealed alloy will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the unannealed baseline alloy.
Above 1000°C, the nanoscale precipitates are expected to coarsen.
Above 1000°C, the nanoscale precipitates are expected to lose coherence.
A controlled comparison of annealed and unannealed material can test the proposed precipitate-mediated effects.
The hypothesis is falsified if the annealed alloy shows no improvement in all three performance measures and TEM detects no nanoscale precipitate structure.
